reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 32. Nay or No: 8. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 37 (92%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 210 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

finance.disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
finance.cycle_rule: House filings use the 2026 two-year cycle.
finance.scope_note: Figures are committee receipts and itemized Schedule A for this two-year cycle only. This is not career fundraising. Schedule E outside spending is not included.
finance.contributor_note: Itemized Schedule A receipts for this principal campaign committee and cycle, grouped by contributor name. Memo lines are omitted so an earmark is not counted twice. Unitemized donations are not in this list. Not every Schedule A row was retrieved, so this ranking uses the largest receipts returned and can miss contributors whose gifts are smaller but add up.
finance.pac_note: Committees and party committees among the itemized contributors, largest amounts first. Up to five. Their donors are Schedule A filings of that committee for the same cycle, disclosed donors only.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

America is the greatest nation in the world because of the men and women who have answered the call to defend freedom. Their sacrifice and unfaltering commitment to our country have protected our liberties.

In Alaska, we have a proud military heritage, and our veterans have played an extraordinary role in both defending our nation and serving our communities. From World War II through the Cold War and continuing to this present moment, Alaska’s strategic role in our national defense cannot be understated. Generations of Alaskans coming from every community - whether urban, rural, or the bush - have proudly served our country in uniform. Our state’s connection to America’s defense runs deep.

On Veterans Day, we honor all who have worn our nation’s uniform and recognize the sacrifices made by their families. 

Their legacy reminds us that freedom is never guaranteed, but is secured through the courage and sacrifice of those willing to defend it. May we never take their service for granted, and may we always honor their sacrifices by preserving the freedoms they fought so bravely to protect.

Alaska has lost a true original with the passing of longtime Alaskan entertainer, Mr. Whitekeys. 

His sharp wit and ability to find humor in Alaska politics made him a beloved entertainer and a legend in his own right. I had the pleasure of meeting Mr. Whitekeys in person, and it was easy to see why so many Alaskans admired him. He had a remarkable gift for bringing people together and reminding us that even in the often-serious world of politics, there is always room for a little humor. 

My heartfelt condolences go out to his wife, Judith, his family and the many Alaskans whose lives he touched.

Today marks an historic milestone for Alaska’s transportation infrastructure and economic future.

I was proud to join U.S. Department of Transportation @SecDuffy and @SenDanSullivan to announce $249 million for the Port MacKenzie Rail Extension, a transformational investment that will help create new opportunities for economic growth across our state.

This funding will support the construction of a 32-mile rail connection linking Port MacKenzie to the Alaska Railroad's existing mainline, providing a more direct and efficient route for transporting Alaska's minerals and energy resources to domestic and international markets.

For decades, Alaskans have recognized the tremendous potential of Port MacKenzie. But realizing that potential requires sustained investment and the determination to see critical infrastructure projects through to completion.

As Vice-Chair of the Subcommittee on Railroads and Pipelines in the U.S. House, I have worked to ensure Alaska's unique infrastructure needs remain a priority in Washington. Earlier this year, we helped secure a $34 million federal investment to expand Port MacKenzie's cargo handling capabilities and supporting infrastructure. 

Today's $249 million announcement represents another major step toward building the transportation network necessary to support long-term development at the port. These investments build on one another. Expanding port capacity is essential but connecting that capacity to Alaska's broader transportation network is what will allow us to fully capitalize on the opportunities ahead.

I want to thank Secretary Duffy for recognizing the strategic importance of Alaska's transportation infrastructure, Senator Sullivan for his continued partnership, and the Alaska Railroad Corporation, Matanuska-Susitna Borough, and countless Alaskans who have worked for years to advance this project.

Major infrastructure projects do not happen overnight, and today's announcement is the result of sustained efforts to turn a long-standing vision into reality. 

There is still work ahead, and I remain committed to advancing these investments through the next stages of development and construction.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
